scope: one current-source, minimum-level IR pulse with one in-memory YUV analysis on the connected Lumia 950 XL cityman

device.kernel: installed kernel #29; no reboot or kernel change

app.action: one IR + analyze pulse; frame pixels analyzed in memory then discarded

setup.owner_report: phone in a white thin box
setup.interpretation_limit: This is not a validated eye-safety enclosure or target. No optical power or exposure measurement was made.

camera.preview_mode: manual exposure 29,995,718 ns; ISO 100; frame duration 33,441,782 ns; post-RAW boost 100
camera.sensor_timestamp_source: UNKNOWN (reported as 0); cannot compare sensor time with elapsed-realtime helper events

illumination.prior_driver_mapping: lowest previously measured nonzero torch request; hardware code 1; max_brightness 200

analysis.heuristic_display_proposal: center=(1542,672) sensor px; pupil radius 24 px; iris radius 60 px; edge strengths 0.007/0.003
analysis.proposal_warning: whole-frame contrast heuristic only; display-only and explicitly excluded from matcher; not iris localization

timing_analyzer.interpretation: The request and matching buffer were bracketed by the helper ON/STOP transaction, but UNKNOWN sensor timestamp source prevents cross-clock exposure-overlap calculation; software ordering does not measure optical timing.

comparison.interpretation: The delivered IR-pulse frame has substantially more luma signal than the previous IR-off frame. Because the phone setup/box may have changed between captures and optical output was not measured, the difference is evidence of a useful illuminated frame but not a controlled measurement of emitter gain or eye safety.

limits: One pulse only; no repeated illumination or sensor-strobe use.
The helper's OFF acknowledgement followed STOP by about 846 ms; the script writes brightness zero before waiting for its watchdog child, but LED optical turn-off was not measured.
No reliable eye ROI, iris localization, liveness, matching, Android enrollment, or unlock was demonstrated.
Minimum hardware code and short software duration are not eye-safety validation.
publication: local only; no commit, push or PR
